correctness.summary: Affine normalization reduces every admissible orbit to scalars a=g(1), c=g(a), and t=(c-a)/(a-1). The contraction inequalities force explicit feasible intervals, while the accelerated error is (a-t)/(1-t). Endpoint optimization on the positive and negative branches gives the stated global factor, and continuous piecewise-affine q-contractions attain equality. Adding monotonicity gives the second exact factor. High-precision witness checks and deterministic feasible-region stress tests agree with the proof.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical work on Steffensen convergence, divided differences, monotone enclosure, and a-posteriori bounds was checked together with modern Anderson-acceleration and fixed-point-acceleration literature. No checked source states the same exact global factor, the (1+sqrt(17))/8 universal nonexpansion threshold, the exact nondecreasing factor, or the 16/9 same-evaluation minimax comparison. Full theorem-level text was not available for several older highly relevant papers, especially Schmidt (1966), Johnson-Scholz (1968), Hofmann (1975), and Schneider (1981), leaving residual historical-equivalence uncertainty.

value.summary: The result gives an exact robustness frontier for classical scalar acceleration, separates smooth local acceleration from worst-case global contraction behavior, identifies sharp stability thresholds, and shows that the accelerated two-evaluation cycle has a strictly worse minimax error guarantee than two unaccelerated Picard evaluations under bare contraction information.

limitations: Exact arithmetic only; floating-point cancellation in Aitken extrapolation is not analyzed.
The main theorem is a one-cycle fixed-point-error statement.
No vector, Hilbert-space, or Anderson-acceleration analogue is claimed.
Failure of the universal threshold does not imply long-run divergence.
Several older highly relevant papers were not available at full theorem level, leaving residual originality uncertainty.
Independent audit has not been performed.
